clue.text: It shouldn't be dangerous, but note: one false move ...

indicators.note: a move shifts things about, so the word it follows is rearranged

blocks.note: fa (fah) is a note of the sol-fa scale
the Roman numeral for one
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning about some hazard: one wrong step and disaster follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A fail-safe mechanism is designed so that any breakdown leaves things in a harmless state rather than a hazardous one.

clue.text: See 12
Range of Ford models?

blocks.note: first meaning: a mountain range with a jagged profile
second meaning: a family car Ford sold through the 1980s and 1990s

explanation.surface: Someone asks about the line-up of cars a manufacturer offers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Range' looks like a product range of cars, but it is the mountain sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A sierra is a long jagged chain of mountains, and the Ford Sierra was a popular saloon car model.

clue.text: Blackwidow.com?

blocks.note: surface reading: an internet address for something called Blackwidow
setter's reading: the black widow is a spider, and its home is a web, so this is where it sits

explanation.walkthrough: The dot-com makes you think of an internet address, which it also is; the joke is that a spider's place really is a web.
explanation.definitionFit: An internet page address is a location on the web, and a black widow spider's location is literally its web.

clue.text: The marine creature is fairly quick, according to Spooner

indicators.note: Dr Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so the sounds of the phrase are exchanged

blocks.note: fairly quick is fast-ish; Spooner swaps its opening F with the ST sound in its middle

explanation.surface: A remark that some sea animal moves at a decent pace.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech STAR and STA- sound alike, so swapping the sounds F and ST in fast-ish gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A starfish is a sea-dwelling echinoderm with five arms, plainly a creature of the ocean.

clue.text: Say "you naughty beast" in farewell to the variety show

indicators.note: say asks for a word as it is spoken, so a single letter that sounds like it stands in
in places one thing within another, so the first part sits inside the word for goodbye

blocks.note: the letter U is pronounced like this word
a mischievous person is a little devil
vale is Latin for goodbye, used in English too

explanation.surface: Someone bids a cheeky farewell, calling out a playful insult, as an old music-hall show closes.
explanation.walkthrough: Vale is the Latin word for goodbye, still used in English; the spoken 'you' needs only its letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Vaudeville is a theatrical entertainment made up of a mix of song, dance and comic acts, the American music hall.

clue.text: Calling for speed

blocks.note: first meaning: one's profession or vocation
second meaning: to rush along headlong, as a verb

explanation.walkthrough: 'Calling for speed' reads like demanding haste; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A calling is a lifelong occupation, and to career is to move swiftly and uncontrollably.

clue.text: Get up off yours and cheer on the team!

definitions.note: in 'get up off yours', yours stands for the thing you sit on

blocks.note: to back a team is to support it
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: A rallying call to a lazy spectator: stand up and support your team!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get up off yours' is a polite stand-in for 'get up off your bottom'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'get up off your backside' means stop sitting, so yours here is one's rear or bottom.

clue.text: Something suspicious smelt returns to pinch one crown

indicators.note: something that returns goes back the way it came, so the phrase is read from the end
to pinch is to grab and hold, so the result holds a letter inside it

blocks.note: when you suspect foul play you smell a rat
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone senses something fishy as a thief tries to steal a crown.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled ornamental headband, a kind of small crown worn by women.

clue.text: Revolutionary Guardian rebels - editor's heading off to the right to find himself

indicators.note: a heading sits at the top, so only the opening letter of the word is kept
going off to somewhere means leaving one place for another, so one letter departs and another takes its place
a revolution overturns the existing order, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of the word for the newspaper's chief
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Rebels at the Guardian newspaper rise up, and their editor heads off to the right politically to find himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the E in the fodder for R, then rearrange. Alan Rusbridger was editing the Guardian, the paper this puzzle ran in, when it was set.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue points at the paper's own editor of the time, so 'himself' means that very man, named in full.

clue.text: See 10
Potential downfall of family requiring asylum?

blocks.note: someone needing a mental asylum is crazy, or bananas
one's kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: A family seeking refuge faces possible ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Asylum' suggests refugees, but here it is the old word for a mental hospital. The family come after the madness in the answer: bananas kin.
explanation.definitionFit: A banana skin is a slapstick cause of a fall, and figuratively any blunder or trap that could cause someone's undoing.

clue.text: Old drug dealer offers a drug to man, Grant

blocks.note: a taken as written, then pot, slang for cannabis
a man is referred to as he
Cary Grant was the Hollywood film star

explanation.surface: A seedy scene in which a dealer pushes narcotics to a man called Grant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old drug dealer' sounds criminal, but it is the historical chemist.
explanation.definitionFit: An apothecary was a historical pharmacist who prepared and sold medicines, so literally a supplier of remedies.

clue.text: One caught by the actual crime

indicators.note: something caught is held within whatever grabbed it, so the letter sits inside the phrase that follows

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
'the very thing' means the actual thing

explanation.surface: A culprit is nabbed by police for the offence itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Thievery is the act of stealing, which is a specific criminal offence.

clue.text: Ruddy British abroad about to retreat

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word before it wraps around the letter

blocks.note: ruddy means reddish in colour
B is the abbreviation for British
abroad can mean out and about, away from home

explanation.surface: Red-faced British tourists overseas are about to turn back.
explanation.definitionFit: A redoubt is a fortified stronghold, a place of refuge to which defenders can withdraw.

clue.text: Fat couch potato standing around, causing an obstruction to motorists

definitions.note: the answer is plural, together forming an obstruction

indicators.note: in a down clue standing up means reading from the bottom, so the word goes backwards
around means surrounding, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: a slob is a lazy, idle person
lard is pig fat

explanation.surface: A fat layabout stands about in the road holding up the traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: Bollards are short posts set in a road or kerb to stop vehicles entering an area.

clue.text: Curtly announce that you're not having any more vegetable

indicators.note: to announce is to say out loud, and curtly means clipped, so a shortened spoken phrase is wanted

blocks.clueFragment: that you're not having any more
blocks.note: 'you shall not' have any more, said quickly with the N clipped

explanation.surface: Someone tersely tells a diner that there will be no second helpings of vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: A brusque 'shall not', the N swallowed, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallot is a small onion-like bulb from the allium family, used in cooking as a vegetable.

clue.text: Date lacks a very soft, soothing influence

indicators.note: something that lacks things is without them, so those letters are taken out

blocks.note: a date is an appointment
taken as written
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very soft

explanation.surface: A tender, gentle date is missing something.
explanation.definitionFit: An ointment is a salve rubbed on the skin to ease pain or irritation, so it calms and heals.

clue.text: Strong drink in free-for-all at artless get-together

indicators.note: less means without, so those letters are removed from the following word

blocks.note: a scrum is a disorderly crush or melee
a party is a social gathering
the word splits as art plus less, and art is the part removed

explanation.surface: Potent liquor flows at a rowdy, unsophisticated gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Artless' looks like an adjective meaning naive, but it splits into art and less. Scrumpy is rough cider from the West Country of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrumpy is a cloudy farmhouse cider known for being very potent alcohol.

clue.text: Heady mixture of pale and chic

indicators.note: a mixture combines things in a jumbled way, so the letters are stirred up

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cocktail of pallid and stylish looks makes for an intoxicating combination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heady' suggests intoxicating, but it is used literally: to do with the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Cephalic is the anatomical adjective meaning relating to the cranium, so heady in a literal sense.

clue.text: P-Prokofiev turns up appearing way out

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means reading from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: Prokofiev's first name Serge, stuttered as the clue stutters

explanation.surface: A stammered name and a composer rising to exit the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The composer Sergei Prokofiev was known in France as Serge; the stammered initial letter in the clue asks for a stammered first name.
explanation.definitionFit: An egress is an exit, a place or means of going out of a building or area.

clue.text: Work that's outstanding, we hear, was a joke for a thousand drachmas a day

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the words are wanted for their sound and not their spelling

blocks.note: money outstanding is money owed
a day's pay is what a Greek might earn, the drachma being the old Greek currency

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at a debt that was trifling for a Greek earning a thousand drachmas daily.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'owed on a Grecian earn' is the title of Keats's poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Ode on a Grecian Urn is a famous poem by John Keats, so it is a literary work.

clue.text: Speak about point that's embellished

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for speaking goes round the letter

blocks.note: to orate is to make a speech
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A speaker talks around a point, padding it out with flourishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornate means elaborately decorated, which is what something adorned with ornament is.

clue.text: See 23
Retiring satisfied with oneself, with toothless grin

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the word is read in the other direction

blocks.note: smug means self-satisfied

explanation.surface: A shy, self-satisfied person smiles without any teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: When a person without teeth smiles, only the pink flesh of the jaw is on show.

clue.text: Catch bird

blocks.note: first meaning: to trick or dupe someone, catching them out
second meaning: a seabird with white and grey plumage

explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch bird' reads as an instruction to trap a bird; the words are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To gull someone is to deceive them, and a gull is a common seabird.

clue.text: Fliers in pub sent round for a costly fiddle

indicators.note: something sent round turns back on itself, so the word runs the other way

blocks.note: darts are thrown across the pub, the classic pub game

explanation.surface: Pub-goers are scammed in some expensive swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' looks like a con, but it is the violin.
explanation.definitionFit: A Strad, short for Stradivarius, is a violin made by Antonio Stradivari and worth millions.

clue.text: Pouting, having to blow instrument held the wrong way round

indicators.note: the wrong way round means backwards, so the instrument's name is read from its end
something held is gripped inside another, so the instrument goes within the breathing word

blocks.note: a lute is a stringed instrument
to pant is to blow, breathing hard

explanation.surface: A sulky musician has to play a wind instrument upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Pouting is pushing out the lips in sulky displeasure, which is how a petulant person behaves.
